Optionally allow Luma to read step totals from Health Connect. Tap Import to refresh the last seven calendar dates, including today so far. Totals stay on this device and appear in Today, Timeline and saved summaries. Health Connect combines overlapping sources. Luma does not write health data or read sleep or workouts.

Luma stores imported daily step totals in its private local database. It does not upload them, use telemetry, or enable automatic backup. Imports run only while the app is open. Turning imports off stops Luma reads and keeps saved history; manage Health Connect access to revoke permission. Successful imports reconcile corrections and removed data in the last seven dates. Older saved totals remain snapshots. Missing data is shown as unavailable, not zero. Clearing Luma’s app storage or uninstalling deletes these local copies without changing Health Connect data.

This replaces all saved life records, catalogs, and imported history with this backup. Export your current data first if you want to keep it. App language and Android permissions stay as they are. Imports will be turned off.

Life records, names and private photo copies stay in Luma’s private storage on this device. Luma has no account, ads or telemetry and makes no network requests. Core capture and browsing work without optional permissions.

Usage Access optionally reads app names and foreground usage; enabled imports can refresh in the background. Health Connect access is optional and reads only daily step totals while Luma is open. Luma does not write health data. Turning imports off prevents new import requests and keeps saved history. A usage query already in progress may finish; its results are discarded while imports stay off. Use the integration’s Android settings to manage or revoke permission. Photos use the system picker; Luma copies selected images into private storage without broad media access.

Automatic cloud backup and device transfer are disabled. Manual backups include private records and photos and are not encrypted. Your chosen document provider controls where exports are stored. Deleting Luma’s local data does not delete exported backups or original photos and provider records. Manage those copies separately.

Reset Luma to remove all saved life records, catalogs, imported history, private photos, unsaved drafts, caches and app preferences. Luma will close. Export a backup first if you want to keep your data.

This cannot be undone. Android will reset Luma’s app data and close Luma, including removing saved records, private photos, drafts and settings. Export a backup first if needed. This does not delete shared backup files, original photos, Android usage history or Health Connect records. Android also resets runtime permissions and file-access grants.
Android accepted the reset request. Luma will close; open it again after it closes.
Android could not start the reset. Try again, or open Luma’s Android settings and use Storage → Clear storage. Device policies may restrict deletion.
Android app settings are unavailable on this device.

This access is optional. Cancelling keeps capture and browsing available. Turning imports off keeps saved data and does not revoke Android permission. Manage access in Android settings; delete local copies from Privacy and local data.

Turning imports off prevents new import requests and cancels scheduled refreshes. It keeps saved history and does not revoke Android Usage access. A usage query already in progress may finish; its results are discarded while imports stay off. Use Manage access to revoke it.
Missing measurements are unavailable; a saved zero remains zero.
Counts describe people and places linked to saved entries, not time together or visits.
